annotationRationale: The question asks for all positive integer solutions of a bill-value equation. The main route uses parity and disjoint cases; the alternative uses denomination bundles and separators. Those counting techniques remain specific to their respective methods.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is appropriate because the requested result counts all admissible collections.

review.questionCheck: The positive bill counts yield 21 collections, choice B. Collections are counted by denomination counts rather than bill order. The statement, choices, and key are consistent.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Both useful accessible routes are present: parity with disjoint cases, and positive compositions with separators. The supplied generating-function fragment adds no suitable complete AMC 10 route.
review.annotationCheck: Integer-equation solving is appropriately assessed, and cnm_027 supports translating bill values into an expression. Case addition and separators appropriately remain method-specific.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is appropriate because the requested result counts all admissible collections.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The equation forces b=2t with t≥1 and a=5(8−t−c). Positivity is equivalent to t+c≤7. For c=1 through 6, the counts are 6 through 1, totaling 21. Each pair determines exactly one valid collection.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The reduction matches LIVE and the finite enumeration is supported by AoPS casework. The prose explains the argument independently and correctly uses source-informed-original.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The parity observation motivates the substitution. The positivity bound, exhaustive cases, and absence of double counting are explicit.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Integer-solution restrictions, congruence modulo 2 through parity, and the addition principle are all directly used by the three immediate nodes.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: cnm_h230's exact CN topic link fits the disjoint cases. The local integer-equation and congruence nodes have no accepted CN links. Question support cnm_027 appropriately covers expression modeling.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The immediate nodes have no accepted US links. Question support cnm_027 offers variable-expression overlap with 6.EE.B.6, 6.EE.A.2a, and the writing component of 6.EE.A.2; 5.OA.A.2 remains partial. These do not cover the integer-solution count.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All immediate nodes are evidenced, with integer-equation solving central and parity and case addition serving the written route.

methodReviews.mathCheck: 20a must be a common multiple of 20 and 50, hence a multiple of 100, so a=5d. The remaining equation forces b=2e. Valid collections correspond bijectively to positive triples d+e+c=8. Two distinct internal gaps among seven give exactly 21 triples.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: AoPS Solutions 1 and 4 support the composition and bundling ideas. The candidate independently justifies the grouping restrictions and separator correspondence, with the correct nonofficial source-informed-original basis.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The proposed bundling motivates the divisibility work. Both the bill-to-triple correspondence and the positive-group separator construction are explained at use; no unexplained stars-and-bars theorem is required.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All four nodes are direct: integer-equation restrictions, LCM(20,50), separator counting, and the evaluation of the combination number.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact CN links for cnm_p159 and cnm_h237 fit the LCM and combination computations. The local integer-equation and separator nodes have no accepted CN links.

nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The immediate nodes precisely represent the divisibility reduction and the separator count; neither synthesis node replaces the specific procedures.
